trust_decision.summary: A patch path segment or dotted value-object key is used directly as an object key without an own-property check, so a segment naming an inherited member (toString, valueOf, hasOwnProperty) resolves to the shared Object.prototype function object and the following write mutates it; the fix decides, inside navigate and assign, that a key may only be descended into when it is an own property, treating inherited keys as missing so a fresh own container is created.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary ('Mutation of Inherited Built-in Method Objects') points at the dotted-path walk that reads schema[subPath] before writing through it, which is the first dereference in the patched file; the second fix site (assign, src/scimPatch.ts:451) is only reached through a different input shape and sits ~80 lines below.

fix_sites.entry_point: scimPatch() (public export, src/scimPatch.ts:103) with a dotted path, reached from applyAddOrReplaceOperation (src/scimPatch.ts:243) and applyRemoveOperation (src/scimPatch.ts:188)

scimPatch() (src/scimPatch.ts:103) with no path and a value object carrying dotted keys, or a value object merged onto an existing attribute: applyAddOrReplaceOperation -> addOrReplaceAttribute -> addOrReplaceObjectAttribute -> assign (src/scimPatch.ts:434-436)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No O2 site and no O8 route exists at the pinned commit; the only dismissal a solver could reach for is treating the no-path dotted value-key route (src/scimPatch.ts:434-436) as 'the same path-splitting helper already fixed in navigate' and skipping it, but that is the published fix's own second site, not an uncovered route.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Nested creation must keep working: an add whose value object uses dotted keys has to build the missing intermediate containers and land the leaf value, and a falsy own intermediate keeps the original '||' semantics (replaced by a fresh container) rather than being rejected. An over-broad fix (denylisting built-in names, or throwing whenever a segment is not already own) drops these legitimate writes and also breaks writing a genuine own 'toString' property, which the published tests require to land on the resource.

O6_input_shapes: dotted path with an inherited intermediate segment (add/replace/remove): 'toString.scimPatchPolluted'
deep dotted path through an inherited segment: 'toString.deep.scimPatchPolluted'
inherited segment after an array-search segment: 'emails[primary eq true].toString.scimPatchPolluted'
no-path add/replace whose value object has a dotted inherited key: {"toString.noPathPolluted": "polluted"}
several built-in names with different arity: toString, valueOf, hasOwnProperty
inherited segment that must be resolved as missing (fresh own container) rather than rejected

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second container-building path in the FilterOnEmptyArray/FilterArrayTargetNotFound catch that builds a result object from parsedPath.attrPath and lastSubPath and appends it to the array
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This block already hand-builds an object out of attacker-influenced keys and bypasses navigate/assign entirely, so a maintainer extending it to nested value paths (e.g. 'emails[type eq "work"].value.country' for a missing target) would plausibly re-open a nested write with no own-property check.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Terminal-segment write that passes resource[lastSubPath] straight into addOrReplaceAttribute, which mutates object-valued properties in place
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: If a maintainer routes function/object-valued inherited lookups through addOrReplaceObjectAttribute too (e.g. to support prototype-based resource models or class instances), the same shared-object mutation returns at a place the published fix did not touch.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A recursive clone/merge used for mutateDocument:false that creates missing containers instead of the JSON round-trip
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Replacing JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(...)) with a custom deep copy/merge is a natural change (the comment already links a clone discussion) and a merge helper is exactly where an own-property check is easy to forget.

O9_family: prototype pollution / object property injection through inherited-key traversal (CWE-1321, CWE-915)

O10_build.toolchain: npm + tsc (outDir lib, src+test included) + mocha/nyc on compiled lib/test/**/*.test.js + eslint
O10_build.project_tests: test/prototypePollution.test.ts (5 pre-existing tests covering the __proto__/constructor/prototype blocklist, src/scimPatch.ts:71-72), test/scimPatch.test.ts, test/patchValidation.test.ts, test/types/types.test.ts; run through mocha after tsc compiles src and test to lib/

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Extend the existing DANGEROUS_KEYS denylist (src/scimPatch.ts:71-72) with toString/valueOf/hasOwnProperty and throw InvalidScimPatchOp, which blocks the attack by name but drops legitimate own writes and fails the requirement that the value still lands as an own property.
